title: The iron condor
summary: Two credit spreads around the price: premium from both sides, a capped loss on both, and margin close to one spread's.

options: A bull put spread plus a bear call spread
A sold strangle with no protection
questions.why: One spread below the price and one above it.

questions.q: It makes its full profit when the stock at expiry is:
questions.why: Both sold options expire worthless and you keep the whole credit.

questions.q: Why can only one side of a condor lose at expiry?
options: The stock can't be below the puts and above the calls at once
questions.why: The price ends in one place, so at most one spread is in trouble.

questions.q: Put gap 20, call gap 20, lot 250, total credit ₹2,000. Worst case?
One side is tested by a strong move. The disciplined response is:
options: Move the sold strike further out to give it room
Let the stop-loss close that side
Sell more on the tested side
questions.why: Moving or adding to a tested side turns a capped loss into a bigger one.
